title: Slider
summary: A slider allows users to select a value or range of values by moving handles along a track.

columns.content:
Use a slider when users benefit from adjusting a value visually.    
It works well when:

- The value is part of a continuous or stepped range, such as volume, amount or intensity.
- Adjusting and exploring the value is more important than entering a precise number.

The slider can be adjusted using pointer, touch or keyboard.

- Moving the handle updates the value according to the defined step.
- The value indicator displays the current value while the slider is being adjusted.
- The slider should provide immediate visual feedback as the value changes.

A slider can be used to select a single value or a range between two values. Both types can use steps to define the interval between selectable values. Choose a minimum, maximum and step that match the scale and level of precision users need. For example, a slider from 0 to 100 with a step of 5 allows values such as 0, 5, 10 and 15. 

- Single value – uses one handle to select a value between a defined minimum and maximum.
- Range – uses two handles to select a lower and upper value within a defined minimum and maximum.

overview.title: Value display
overview.section-content: By default, the slider includes a textbox that displays the selected value and allows users to enter a precise value. The textbox can be omitted when the selected value or its effect is clearly displayed elsewhere in the interface. For example, adjusting an interest rate could update a monthly cost displayed in a separate summary or card.

columns.content:
### Textbox 

For a single-value slider, one textbox displays the selected value. For a range slider, two textboxes display the selected lower and upper values. The slider and textbox should always stay synchronised. Changing the value in either one should update the other.

### Value indicator 

A bubble appears next to the handle while the slider is being adjusted. It displays the current value and updates as the handle moves. For a range slider, the value indicator displays the value of the handle currently being adjusted.
